overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation in the Board's July 29, 2020 Zoom hearing on a special permit. It declined to review the motion-procedure allegation as outside the law. The Board's own voluntary training was noted but not ordered.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Board's July 29 Zoom meeting did not give the public adequate alternative means of access under the COVID-19 Executive Order.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board provided adequate alternative means of access to the meeting via Zoom as the public could clearly hear the proceedings live.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the applicant was not given an adequate opportunity to present his special permit application at the virtual hearing.
allegations.key_passage: As the Open Meeting Law leaves public participation to the discretion of the public body's chair, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law in this respect.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Board's roll call vote on the applicant's special permit was improper.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board's roll call vote was proper and did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint that a Board member, the Chair, was muted or went off camera for part of the virtual meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to find a violation of the Open Meeting Law where, as here, video technology is generally in use for a meeting, but some members of the public body are not visible at all times.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the motion to take a vote on the application was not properly made by Board members.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.
